title: MuJoCo CPU vs NVIDIA PhysX (Isaac Sim 6.2): can the ballbot be ported?
note: Simulation only. No hardware claims. PhysX has no anisotropic friction; the PhysX model uses a ring of passive rollers per wheel as an emulation (see REPORT.md).

clips.title: LQR hold, robot dropped 2 cm onto the ball
clips.description: Robot and ball dropped 2 cm from the settled pose with the LQR holding zero command. Compares the ball and wheel contact transient and the contact forces.
engines: PhysX 5 (Isaac Sim 6.2), roller-ring omni wheel emulation
clips.outcome: MuJoCo: stays upright, mean speed 0.00 m/s (cmd 0.00), max tilt 1.3 deg, mean wheel-ball normal force 17.6 N; PhysX: stays upright, mean speed 0.00 m/s (cmd 0.00), max tilt 0.4 deg, mean wheel-ball normal force 18.5 N

clips.title: Open-loop torque pulse, 0.5 Nm on wheels 0 and 2 for 0.1 s (0.3x speed)
clips.description: No feedback: 0.5 Nm on wheels 0 and 2 for 0.1 s after 0.1 s of rest. The unstable plant is only comparable for the first 0.3 s; ball and body response is the check.
engines: PhysX 5 (Isaac Sim 6.2), roller-ring omni wheel emulation
clips.outcome: MuJoCo: stays upright, mean speed 0.05 m/s (cmd 0.00), max tilt 13.7 deg, mean wheel-ball normal force 17.5 N; PhysX: stays upright, mean speed 0.07 m/s (cmd 0.00), max tilt 14.9 deg, mean wheel-ball normal force 18.3 N

clips.title: LQR, 1x body-weight 50 ms push at 1.5 s

clips.title: PhysX naive import (isotropic capsule wheels), 0.4 scaled speed
clips.description: What a plain MJCF to PhysX conversion gives: capsule wheels with one isotropic friction coefficient (the anisotropic <pair friction> cannot be represented). Failure case.
clips.outcome: MuJoCo: stays upright, mean speed 0.40 m/s (cmd 0.40), max tilt 9.8 deg, mean wheel-ball normal force 17.8 N; PhysX naive: fell at 0.39 s, mean wheel-ball normal force nan N
